Staged L

A Staged Development Model for Immature Mosquitoes

Source: vignettes/L-stages.Rmd
L-stages.Rmd

The stages model of aquatic mosquito ecology tracks development through six compartments: eggs (EE), four larval instars (L1L_1–L4L_4), and pupae (PP). Each larval instar has its own maturation rate, density-dependent maturation delay, density-independent mortality, and density-dependent mortality. All density-dependent effects act through a weighted mean crowding index.

Differential Equations

Let η\eta denote the egg laying rate from the adult mosquito component and let

L=w1L1+w2L2+w3L3+L4L = w_1 L_1 + w_2 L_2 + w_3 L_3 + L_4

be the weighted mean crowding index. The fourth instar serves as the reference (w4=1w_4 = 1); setting all wi=1w_i = 1 recovers unweighted total larval density.

The dynamical system is:

dE/dt=η−(ψE+ϕE)EdL1/dt=ψEE−ψ1L1e−ξ1L−(ϕ1+θ1L)L1dL2/dt=ψ1L1e−ξ1L−ψ2L2e−ξ2L−(ϕ2+θ2L)L2dL3/dt=ψ2L2e−ξ2L−ψ3L3e−ξ3L−(ϕ3+θ3L)L3dL4/dt=ψ3L3e−ξ3L−ψ4L4e−ξ4L−(ϕ4+θ4L)L4dP/dt=ψ4L4e−ξ4L−(ϕP+ψP)P \begin{array}{rl} dE/dt & = \eta - (\psi_E + \phi_E)\, E \\[4pt] dL_1/dt & = \psi_E E \;-\; \psi_1 L_1\, e^{-\xi_1 L} \;-\; (\phi_1 + \theta_1 L)\, L_1 \\[4pt] dL_2/dt & = \psi_1 L_1\, e^{-\xi_1 L} \;-\; \psi_2 L_2\, e^{-\xi_2 L} \;-\; (\phi_2 + \theta_2 L)\, L_2 \\[4pt] dL_3/dt & = \psi_2 L_2\, e^{-\xi_2 L} \;-\; \psi_3 L_3\, e^{-\xi_3 L} \;-\; (\phi_3 + \theta_3 L)\, L_3 \\[4pt] dL_4/dt & = \psi_3 L_3\, e^{-\xi_3 L} \;-\; \psi_4 L_4\, e^{-\xi_4 L} \;-\; (\phi_4 + \theta_4 L)\, L_4 \\[4pt] dP/dt & = \psi_4 L_4\, e^{-\xi_4 L} \;-\; (\phi_P + \psi_P)\, P \end{array}

The maturation flow leaving instar ii is ψiLie−ξiL\psi_i L_i e^{-\xi_i L}; it feeds directly into the next compartment. Density-dependent delays reduce maturation through the exponential term; density-dependent mortality increases linearly with LL.

The emergence rate of adult female mosquitoes is:

α=ψPP\alpha = \psi_P P

Equilibrium Solutions

Equilibrium values can be computed numerically given an egg deposition rate η\eta using steady_state_L.stages. With ξi=0\xi_i = 0 for all instars, the system is quasi-linear and the solver converges reliably from the starting guess η𝟏6\eta \mathbf{1}_6.

In the common case where all four instars share the same parameters (ψi=ψ\psi_i = \psi, ϕi=ϕ\phi_i = \phi, θi=θ\theta_i = \theta, wi=1w_i = 1), the instar densities are equal at equilibrium (L1*=L2*=L3*=L4*L_1^* = L_2^* = L_3^* = L_4^*) and the flow through the system is set by the egg hatching rate and the target emergence rate. The density-dependent mortality slope θ\theta can then be treated as the parameter that calibrates the steady-state emergence rate to a desired value.
